name: The Hostage Heir
about: A great house's heir has grown up at your court as your ward. Their lord wants the child back, the child has opinions of their own, and a rival house would like the boy dead.
title: The Ward of {lord.house}

beats.speaker: lord
beats.text: {ward} has grown up at Kingsmere as the crown's ward. {lord} writes for the first time in years: {lord.he} wants {lord.his} heir home.

court.text: {lord} of {lord.house}: "My heir has been the crown's guest long enough, Your Grace. Send {ward} home, and {lord.house} will know the crown trusts it."

options.label: Send {ward} home with honours
options.result: {ward} rides home to {seat} with a royal escort and the King's blessing.

options.label: {ward} stays at Kingsmere
options.result: The King keeps {ward} at court. In {seat}, {lord} stops writing.

options.label: Keep {ward} close, and betroth {ward.him} to the crown's choice
options.result: {ward} is betrothed at court. {lord} sends a cold gift for the wedding.

beats.speaker: ward
beats.text: {ward} is home at {seat}, and talks of the King with warmth. {rival} hears of it and is not pleased.

beats.speaker: lord
beats.text: {lord.house}'s men try to spirit {ward} out of Kingsmere by night. They are taken at the river gate, {ward} with them.

court.text: {rival} of {rival.house}: "{lord.house} tried to steal its heir from under the crown's roof, Your Grace. If that goes unpunished, every ward in the realm will follow."

options.label: Send the men home unharmed, and keep the child
options.result: The men go home with a message: the King understands a father's heart, and keeps the child anyway.

options.label: Hang the men at the river gate
options.result: Five of {lord.house}'s men hang at the river gate. {ward} watches from a window.

options.label: Let the child go home after all
options.hint: {lord.houseName} +15 · the realm sees the crown bend
options.result: The King lets {ward} go. {rival} calls it weakness in every hall that will listen.

beats.speaker: rival
beats.text: A knife is found in {ward}'s bed, and a servant of {rival.house} is gone from the household. Whether it was meant to kill or to warn, {lord} knows whom to blame.

court.text: {lord}: "{rival} sent a knife for my child, Your Grace. Give me justice, or I will take it."

options.label: Fine {rival.house} and guard the heir yourself (150 gold)
options.result: {rival.house} pays a blood fine, and {ward} sleeps behind the King's own guard.

options.label: There is no proof
options.result: The King finds no proof. {lord} finds it sufficient.

beats.speaker: lord
beats.text: {lord.house} marches on {rival.house} for the knife in the dark. The realm burns from {seat} to {rival.seat}.

beats.speaker: lord
beats.text: {lord} raises {lord.his} banners against the crown that hanged {lord.his} men and kept {lord.his} child, and marches on Kingsmere to take {ward} back by the sword.

beats.speaker: ward
beats.text: {ward} comes of age loyal to the crown that raised {ward.him}, and {lord.house} with {ward.him}. {thread} ends in a debt the house means to repay.

memory.ward: The King raised me and kept me safe. My house owes the crown.

beats.speaker: ward
beats.text: {lord}'s host breaks before Kingsmere. {ward} watched it from the walls, and will rule {seat} one day knowing what the crown can do.

beats.speaker: lord
beats.text: {ward} dies before coming of age, and the hold the crown had on {lord.house} dies with {ward.him}. {lord} does not forgive it.

beats.speaker: ward
beats.text: {lord} dies, and {ward} rides home from Kingsmere to rule {seat}: a lord raised by the crown.
